name: Neiro Hall
description: An elegant, restrained and cinematic theme for an intimate 180-seat listening hall for chamber music, jazz and acoustic song: a smoke-stone ground and paper cards, charcoal type and dark "hall lights down" bands, warm grey meta text, one muted rust kept to small marks (rules, the active filter, the notch of a ticket stub) and a touch of soft brass, with Space Grotesk in light weights, Inter for text and IBM Plex Mono for dates and seat lines. A slim bar docked to the bottom of the screen carries the wordmark, the menu and a Tickets button on every page. The home page opens on a dark band with the empty hall, then the programme as a filter-first directory of ticket stubs (perforated edge, mono date, seat line) filtered by genre and month with accessible pill buttons; without JavaScript every concert shows. Then the room on a dark band, the ticket prices and the journal. The footer is a programme-booklet colophon: the hall, credits, typefaces and a small contents list. With a full calendar, artists with portraits and a directory, the venue (hall, seating, foyer, access), tickets and box office, about, journal, newsletter and contact. The programme, the ticket prices and the box office details are each edited in one place.
deviation: Planned as a gig-poster look in vivid orange #F15A24 on #1B1B1B and white, with footer F5. Changed at the user's request (elegant, restrained Japanese minimal, no bright colours, no gig-poster or street look): the orange is toned down to a desaturated rust #A5532F kept to small marks (rules, active filter, stub notch; #8A4426 for text links), on smoke stone #ECEAE6, paper #F5F4F1 and charcoal #19191B with warm grey #67635E (darkened slightly from #6F6B66 so meta text passes AA on stone) and soft brass #B39A6E. Style tags elegant + audio + cinematic instead of gig-poster. Footer F9 colophon instead of F5, so the combo does not repeat Menya Kaen v1's H7 + F5. Inter added as the body font.
